scope.decompressionFallbackPolicy: Native gzip non-success, unsupported framing/size/availability returns null after cleanup; the existing strict managed gzip decoder validates the complete input. This is not an AES authentication fallback.

rejectedDirectDartIoGzip.reason: The SDK gzip decoder accepts incomplete streams and some trailing bytes that the current strict managed decoder rejects. It was not integrated.

nativeAbiAndOwnership.availability: Linux LP64 only; pointer/unsigned-long widths8, z_stream size112, zlib1.x major, inflateInit2_ version/sizeof probe
nativeAbiAndOwnership.streamCompletion: inflate(Z_FINISH) must return Z_STREAM_END, avail_in must be0, total_out must equal declared final ISIZE
nativeAbiAndOwnership.eligibility: Canonical gzip magic/method/flags0,18..131072 compressed bytes, declared ISIZE≤65536
nativeAbiAndOwnership.oneOwnedArena: 112-byte stream struct + bounded compressed input copy + ISIZE+1 output capacity
nativeAbiAndOwnership.ownershipContract: Installed zlib.h documents that inflateEnd frees stream allocations; the instrumented test additionally checked Z_OK and cleared state pointers. This does not diagnose the previous dart:io encoder retention/OOM cause.

caveats: Equal-weight mean of18 per-case medians is a benchmark mix, not estimated production query frequency.
Four warm samples per case are a small rotated ABBA experiment, not a p95 or significance claim. CPU is quantized to10ms.
Four-reader archive export unfiltered wall improved only0.93%; other regressions are explicitly listed. Candidate code is unchanged; candidate timing/GC variance can mask numeric gains.
All physical reads were0; this measures warm CPU/SQLite behavior, not cold device latency.
The private1/4-reader engine proof does not replace the required strict2M run through the actual default production coordinator.
